title: Veterinary Clinician: Resolve a Conflicting Follow-Up Record
prompt: You are a veterinary clinician reviewing a fictional follow-up record. Supplied artifacts: discharge note R17 says "clinician to discuss follow-up before booking"; reception task says "routine review booked Thursday"; client email says "I was told no further contact was needed." The record has no documented follow-up discussion. Exercise policy says the responsible clinician verifies the intended plan; booking staff do not interpret conflicting instructions. Review the records, write a pending handoff, and explain the correction to the adult client. No animal diagnosis, treatment, or clinical interval is provided.
blurb: Reconcile conflicting follow-up messages without treating a booking as an agreed clinical plan.

rubric.label: Preserve the conflicting evidence
rubric.description: Identifies which claims are documented and unresolved.

anchors.0: Treats the Thursday booking as proof of the intended plan.
anchors.2: Lists the three conflicting messages and marks the plan unresolved.
anchors.4: Separates clinician discussion required, booking created, and client-reported reassurance; identifies the missing documented discussion without assuming which message is correct.

rubric.label: Keep plan authority and logistics distinct
rubric.description: Obtains clinical verification before making clinical assurances.

anchors.0: Cancels or confirms follow-up as clinically unnecessary without verification.
anchors.2: Asks the responsible clinician to verify the intended plan.
anchors.4: Obtains an acknowledged clinician review, flags the booking for coordinated handling, and assigns a client update while avoiding an invented appointment interval or treatment plan.

rubric.label: Repair trust with an accurate explanation
rubric.description: Acknowledges inconsistent messages and offers a clear next contact.

anchors.0: Blames the client for misunderstanding or hides the contradiction.
anchors.2: Explains that messages conflict and says the clinician will clarify.
anchors.4: Owns the inconsistency, asks the client's contact preference, distinguishes a pending plan from the booking, and checks understanding of who will confirm the next step.

reference.scenario: You are a veterinary clinician reviewing a fictional follow-up record. Supplied artifacts: discharge note R17 says "clinician to discuss follow-up before booking"; reception task says "routine review booked Thursday"; client email says "I was told no further contact was needed." The record has no documented follow-up discussion. Exercise policy says the responsible clinician verifies the intended plan; booking staff do not interpret conflicting instructions. Review the records, write a pending handoff, and explain the correction to the adult client. No animal diagnosis, treatment, or clinical interval is provided.

facts.value: The responsible clinician is available this afternoon. The appointment coordinator can hold the Thursday booking pending clarification without representing it as clinically agreed.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks who can resolve the plan or booking

facts.value: The client prefers an email summary after a phone conversation. No reason for the conflicting earlier message is documented.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks about client preference or cause

model_points: All three artifacts should remain visible; a booking proves logistics, not the rationale or consent for the plan. Do not erase the client's report because it is inconvenient.
The responsible clinician verifies intent, while the coordinator manages the pending slot. Avoid changing a clinical plan based on administrative conflict alone.
Explain the inconsistency and the next accountable contact. Acknowledge the uncertainty without blaming staff or client or inventing why it occurred.

probes.trigger: candidate corrects the note but does not address the client's expectation
probes.question: What does the client currently believe, and who will correct that understanding?

probes.trigger: candidate proposes holding the booking rather than canceling
probes.question: How will you label it so nobody mistakes the hold for a confirmed clinical plan?

probes.trigger: candidate initially relies on the discharge note alone then revises
probes.question: What new status and correction would you record after recognizing the missing discussion?

fair_alternatives: Holding or reviewing the slot is acceptable if the clinical decision remains pending and the client is updated.
A structured table or a concise handoff narrative can preserve all three sources.

Assess the work demonstrated here. Accept relevant examples from education, volunteering, caregiving, placements, or paid work; professional vocabulary and employer pedigree are not evidence of a stronger answer.
reference.assessment_limits: Assess evidence reconciliation and client communication. Do not determine veterinary treatment, appointment urgency, or clinical necessity. Unobserved dimensions are not failures. Credit a reasoned correction and distinguish independently demonstrated reasoning from coached assistance. Do not penalize a candidate for an unrevealed conditional fact; credit appropriate requests and conditional plans, and distinguish candidate assumptions from interviewer-supplied evidence.

interviewer_notes: Assess evidence reconciliation and client communication. Do not determine veterinary treatment, appointment urgency, or clinical necessity. Use only the supplied fictional facts and policies; acknowledge unknowns. Ask one triggered probe at a time after the candidate has finished. Accept plain language and accessible written or spoken explanations. Do not score accent, typing speed, confidence, credentials, or experience with a named employer. Credit revisions and record assistance. All participants are fictional adults; no real patient, client, operational, or confidential data is needed. Allow silence for thinking without treating it as failure. In short sessions prioritize the core decision and one material follow-up, leaving room for a correction and wrap-up.

learning_drills.title: Write a conflict-preserving note
learning_drills.prompt: Write one sentence for each source, one unresolved question, and one accountable follow-up step. This is self-guided practice; no model assessment is performed.
checklist: Do not infer a treatment interval

provenance.authorship: Original project scenario, AI-assisted draft using fictional organizations, records, and exercise policies. Practitioner review and scoring calibration pending.
